target.title: refactor(copilot): use SDK session and tool-result contracts
target.body:
Closes #106192

## What Problem This Solves

Copilot plugin maintenance duplicated contracts already owned by the pinned Copilot SDK: session-compaction configuration and MCP tool-result conversion. The copies added 225 net lines of drift-prone code and tests.

## Why This Change Was Made

Forward `SessionConfig["infiniteSessions"]` directly and use the SDK's public `convertMcpCallToolResult` helper for successful tool output. OpenClaw keeps its own execution-failure and lifecycle-error handling; SDK-owned defaults, validation, and result conversion stay with the SDK.

## User Impact

No intended user-visible behavior change. The Copilot plugin has less local compatibility code and follows the exact pinned SDK contracts.

## Evidence

- Net change: 13 insertions, 238 deletions (225 fewer lines).
- Direct dependency proof: `@github/copilot-sdk` 1.0.5 publicly exports `convertMcpCallToolResult`; `SessionConfig` owns `infiniteSessions`. The pinned Copilot CLI 1.0.68 applies identical defaults for omitted and empty infinite-session config while preserving explicit values.
- Focused Blacksmith Testbox run [29235869371](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29235869371): 193 tests passed across `attempt.test.ts` and `tool-bridge.test.ts`.
- Same Testbox lease: `pnpm check:changed` passed.
- Same Testbox lease: `pnpm build` passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Fresh pre-commit and post-rebase autoreviews: no actionable findings.

AI assistance: Codex audited the dependency contracts, implemented the refactor, and ran validation. Maintainer reviewed the resulting diff and evidence.

target.title: Settings: add unified usage and spend dashboard
target.body:
## Product case

CodexBar has detailed provider views but no single Settings destination that answers three basic questions together: what did I spend, which subscriptions drove it, and which models did I use most? This PR adds a local, spend-first dashboard using CodexBar's existing history rather than a new analytics service.

The intentionally narrow v1 is **local exploration**:

- no upload, telemetry, hosted account, or new persistence format;
- no prompts, projects, paths, emails, or account identities in the dashboard model;
- unknown or unpriced history remains visibly unavailable rather than becoming `$0`;
- 7- and 30-day windows are computed from the same local daily entries.

## What this adds

- A persisted **Usage & Spend** destination in the existing Settings sidebar.
- 7/30-day estimated spend, tracked-token, and priced-history coverage summaries.
- Ranked subscription rows, including distinct identity-free Codex account rows.
- Cross-subscription model rankings and a daily estimated-spend chart.
- Existing CodexBar panels, provider colors/icons, native controls, localization, dark mode, empty states, and reduced-motion behavior.

## Account-complete data contract

`ProviderInput` is subscription-scoped rather than provider-unique. Multiple Codex accounts remain separate rows and all contribute to totals, daily points, and model aggregates.

The active Codex account reuses the normal provider cost snapshot. Each sibling account scans its own Codex home into a separate hashed cache, with Pi session history disabled for sibling scans so shared Pi history is counted exactly once. Failed or unavailable history remains a visible unpriced subscription row.

No account identity, path, project, prompt, or credential crosses into the dashboard presentation model.

## Sanitized native proof

These screenshots use deliberately simulated, sanitized fixtures rendered through the production native Settings view. They exercise distinct Codex accounts, mixed priced/unpriced history, both time windows, light/dark appearance, and the empty state without exposing private data.

### Light - 30 days - mixed priced/unpriced

![Usage and Spend light 30-day dashboard](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Chipagosfinest/CodexBar/b425f6bac051f2bee8e4145b6ff97a1d4138961a/docs/screenshots/usage-spend-dashboard-light-30d.png)

### Dark - 7 days - mixed priced/unpriced

![Usage and Spend dark 7-day dashboard](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Chipagosfinest/CodexBar/b425f6bac051f2bee8e4145b6ff97a1d4138961a/docs/screenshots/usage-spend-dashboard-dark-7d.png)

### Empty/unpriced history

![Usage and Spend empty dashboard](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Chipagosfinest/CodexBar/b425f6bac051f2bee8e4145b6ff97a1d4138961a/docs/screenshots/usage-spend-dashboard-empty.png)

## Relationship to sharing

- Companion draft: [#2112 - Add local shareable usage card](https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar/pull/2112)
- This PR owns persistent in-app exploration only.
- #2112 owns export/share actions only.
- Neither branch depends on the other at build or runtime.

## Why a dedicated pane

This remains a draft because the top-level destination is a product decision, not an implementation inevitability. A dedicated pane avoids overloading provider settings or the menu, provides enough width for aligned comparisons, and keeps trend analysis out of the fast-glance path. If maintainers prefer an existing shared overview, the aggregation model can survive while presentation moves.

## Verification

- [x] `swift build`
- [x] `swift test --filter UnifiedSpendDashboardModelTests` - 3 focused tests passed, including two distinct Codex subscriptions contributing to totals and model aggregation
- [x] `make check`
- [x] Production target compiles after the account-complete repair
- [x] Sanitized native proof: light/dark, 7/30-day, mixed/unpriced, and empty states
- [ ] Full sharded suite in fresh CI

The local bundled-app widget step is blocked by an installed Xcode `IDESimulatorFoundation` / `DVTDownloads` plug-in mismatch. This is machine-local; the CodexBar app target builds cleanly, and the PR's fresh GitHub CI is the authoritative bundle/test result.

## Product/design decision requested

`VISION.md` requires sign-off for new product surfaces. The implementation, account-completeness blocker, and inspectable proof are now addressed. This draft asks whether CodexBar should keep a permanent top-level spend-first dashboard or present the same aggregation inside an existing shared overview.
